response.reason: The cited clause, Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Art. 22(1)(a), establishes that a quantitative indication (QUID) is required when an ingredient appears in the name of the food or is usually associated with that name. The verdict turns on this requirement, stating that 'apple juice concentrate' appears in the name and that the quantitative declaration is provided. The clause is directly relevant and supports the legal grounding of the verdict.
